blocks.text: What's Happening in Brookswood Right Now

parts.t: The biggest planning shift in Brookswood's history is underway. Here is what changed and what it means.

Brookswood is in the midst of its most significant transformation in decades. After years of remaining largely single-family in character, the Township of Langley's adoption of Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (
SSMUH
) rules and a revamped Official Community Plan have fundamentally changed what is possible on almost every residential lot in the area.
This is not a distant plan. Rezoning applications are already in motion, lots with development potential are trading at premiums, and the Township designated Brookswood-Fernridge as its
next major area of growth after Willoughby
November 2024
Langley Township — the last municipality in Metro Vancouver to act — adopted
Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 6020
, introducing a new "Houseplex" category. Up to 4 units are now permitted on most serviced single-family lots.
2025 Update
The Township updated its OCP and the Brookswood-Fernridge Neighbourhood Plans (Booth, Fernridge, Rinn) to align with SSMUH rules. An Engineering Capacity Study for water and sewer is also underway.
December 2025
Council approved 3 readings for 60 SSMUH structures on a 13.7-acre Brookswood site — potentially up to 240 units if built as fourplexes. Developer committed a $1.17M Community Amenity Contribution.
February 2026
A 37-lot subdivision on the 19800-block of 32 Avenue received preliminary approval, zoned for single-family to fourplexes — potentially 37 to 148 total units depending on final configuration.
What Is an SSMUH?
SSMUH

stands for Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing — a three-plex, four-plex, or six-plex built on a previously single-family lot. Most serviced Brookswood lots can now accommodate up to 4 units. ALR properties are excluded entirely.
3-plex
Smaller Lots
Lots below minimum size thresholds can still accommodate a three-plex under the new Houseplex rules.
4-plex
Most Standard Lots
The majority of serviced residential lots in Brookswood can now accommodate up to four dwelling units.
6-plex
Transit-Adjacent Lots
Lots near frequent transit corridors may qualify for up to six units — the maximum under SSMUH rules.
The development premium, and how it applies differently depending on the parcel.
Brookswood is currently a
buyer's market

— more active listings than buyers purchasing, which gives buyers real negotiating leverage on turnkey family homes. But that average hides a split. Lots with confirmed development potential are a separate market, and they are commanding premiums well above the neighbourhood median.
Important — Environmental Protections
The revised neighbourhood plans expanded environmental protection areas —
27% of the entire Brookswood-Fernridge community
is now designated as protected. Creek greenways and SPEA setbacks directly reduce buildable lot area on some properties. Verify before buying or selling with development intent.
Brookswood-Fernridge is divided into three plan areas — Booth, Fernridge, and Rinn — each with distinct land use designations.
North Brookswood

Covers the northern section of Brookswood-Fernridge. Revised in 2024–2025 to accommodate SSMUH zoning. A 12-acre school and park site dedication (6 acres each) is required before broader development in the area proceeds.
Township Info →
Central Area

The most active area for development applications right now — both the 60-unit SSMUH project and the 37-lot subdivision sit within this zone. The Fernridge NCP includes areas designated at 10,000 SF lots. CAC rates were reduced 10–15% in the 2024 revisions, making development more financially viable.
Township Info →
South Brookswood

Covers the southern section. The Rinn NCP was revised alongside the 2025 OCP update to align with SSMUH rules. Properties closer to the ALR boundary need careful due diligence on agricultural land status before any development assumptions are made.

blocks.text: Your Property Has Three Values Right Now

parts.t: A standard home evaluation only ever tells you the first one.
i
What a family buyer pays for the house as it stands. This is the number a typical evaluation gives you — and in the current buyer's market, it is the softest of the three.
ii
What a small builder pays for a site supporting three, four, or six units. Depends on lot size, servicing capacity, and whether a creek setback eats into buildable area.
iii
What a developer pays when your lot is combined with neighbouring ones. Often the highest number — and the one that depends most on timing and on who else is willing.
These do not always rank the way you would expect.

A property with a creek greenway or SPEA setback can be worth more as a home than as a lot. One near a frequent transit corridor can be worth far more as a lot than the house would ever fetch. It comes down to the specific parcel — which is the whole point of getting it assessed.

Can I build a fourplex on my Brookswood lot?

Most serviced single-family lots in Brookswood can now accommodate up to four units under Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 2024. ALR-designated properties are excluded. What a specific parcel actually supports comes down to lot size, servicing capacity, and whether a creek or SPEA setback reduces the buildable area.
What is an SSMUH in Langley?

Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing — a three-plex, four-plex, or six-plex on a lot that was previously single-family. Langley Township adopted Houseplex zoning in November 2024, the last municipality in Metro Vancouver to do so, which is part of why Brookswood is only now seeing the applications that other areas saw earlier.
Is Brookswood in the ALR?

The developed residential core is not, but some properties near the boundaries are — particularly in the southern Rinn plan area. ALR status overrides SSMUH eligibility entirely, so it is the first thing to confirm before making any development assumption about a parcel.
How is lot value different from home value?

Home value is what a family buyer pays for the house as it stands. Lot value is what a builder pays for a site that supports multiple units. Since the SSMUH rules came in, these can be very different numbers for the same property — and which is higher depends on the parcel, not on the neighbourhood average.
Is my lot part of a land assembly area?

Assembly interest is concentrated in the Fernridge plan area and along the 200 Street corridor, where the largest applications have been filed. Whether a specific lot is in demand depends on its position relative to those sites and on whether neighbouring owners are willing. Assembly value only exists if the neighbours are on board, which is why timing matters more here than in an ordinary sale.
Should I sell now or wait?

Honest answer: it depends which of the three values applies to your property, and nobody can tell you that without looking at the specific parcel. Turnkey family homes are facing a buyer's market with real negotiating pressure. Lots with confirmed development potential are a different market entirely. Waiting helps in one of those situations and costs you in the other.
